From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@finservco.com>

Cc: Security Incident Response <sir@finservco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure - EU scope?

Team —

Our monitoring flagged an anomalous outbound request pattern from a Redwood ingestion endpoint that processes EU user telemetry. We saw repeated GETs to an internal debug path between 02:00-03:00 UTC; payload samples attached (audit-log-export.csv, screenshot-headers.png). At first glance it looks like a misconfigured forwarding rule, but we need your confirmation on whether any customer-identifying fields were included in the payloads.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the affected flow contains PII or user identifiers?
- Which subprocessors (if any) touched the raw logs in the last 48 hours?
- Can you preserve logs and not delete rotation for 14 days while we triage?

We are particularly sensitive because a subset of impacted users are EU residents — any notification windows or cross-border transfer constraints matter. Please escalate to legal as needed.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Principal Security Ops
FinServCo

Attachments: audit-log-export.csv (text/csv), screenshot-headers.png (image/png)

Thanks Alice — I’m pulling the incident team together.

Actions we are kicking off now:
- Ben will snapshot ingestion logs and preserve them in a secure evidence bucket (retain 14 days) — do not rotate.
- Kimberly will confirm the subprocessor roster and whether any contracts require immediate notification.
- I’ll ask CS and the on-call SRE to create a short-lived read-only access for your SIR team if you need to pull artifacts.

Proposed timeline (subject to legal guidance):
- Initial scope confirmation (classification of data types): 24 hours
- Forensic-ready evidence bundle: 72 hours
- If EU personal data is confirmed, prepare notification materials and coordination plan within 72 hours to align with DPA obligations ("without undue delay and no later than 72 hours" phrasing is our default starting point) — legal to confirm exact language.

Please confirm whether FinServCo needs a forensic vendor engaged under NDA and whether transfer requests to subprocessors are allowed under your engagement terms.

Triage owners: Ben Carter (technical), Kimberly Park (subprocessors/contracts), Marissa Cole (legal liaison).

—

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure - EU scope? (legal input)

Importance: High

Thanks for the rapid response. A few legal notes to guide triage and notification planning:
- Contractual/DPA framing: our standard DPA references both "notify without undue delay" and an explicit 72-hour window for supervisory authority notification in certain jurisdictions. For customer notification obligations, timing may vary by country and by the regulator — we should treat 72 hours as the target for readiness, not necessarily public notification.
- Subprocessors: review SubprocDataFlow Inc.'s subprocessor agreement. If they processed personal data, per our DPA we must obtain cooperation for evidence export within 48 hours and, where feasible, provide a signed statement of facts for the customer.
- Cross-border transfers: if any of the retained logs include full IP addresses or other identifiers that would trigger GDPR transfer rules, we need to evaluate SCC applicability and whether we require export consent or a lawful transfer mechanism.

Please confirm the following ASAP:
1) Is the affected cohort EU-resident-only, or mixed region?
2) Do the payloads include raw IP addresses or other direct identifiers (not hashed)?
3) Do we have any contractual limits that prohibit SubprocDataFlow from sharing forensic exports with FinServCo or with an approved forensic vendor?

I’ve looped in Jacob (external counsel) to advise on cross-border phrasing and whether to engage a forensic vendor under our existing NDA.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

- Subprocessors: SubprocDataFlow Inc. and EU-Logs Ltd. may have transient copies. Kimberly confirmed SubprocDataFlow has a cooperation clause but requires a written request and 48-hour turnaround for exports.

Notification timeline (tentative):
- T+24h: scope memo for FinServCo legal (done).
- T+72h: forensic-ready bundle and draft notification materials for supervisory authority / customer, contingent on legal sign-off.
- T+7 days: follow-up evidence handover and confirm whether public notification is needed after regulator guidance.

Action items and owners:
- Ben Carter: finalize forensic bundle; mark logs as preserved and share secure link. (owner)
- Kimberly Park: send formal subprocessor export request to SubprocDataFlow and confirm turnaround. (owner)
- Marissa Cole & Jacob Myers: finalize notification wording and advise on SCC/transfer language. (owner)
- Sean Gallagher: coordinate with CS to prepare customer comm template and coordinate any required credits/SLAs. (owner)

Requests for FinServCo:
- Please confirm whether you want Redwood to share raw forensic images with your chosen vendor, or if you prefer Redwood to produce a curated packet.
- If you prefer a vendor, please provide vendor contact and signed access authorization (we can accept DocuSign).

We will hold all evidence in the secure bucket and will not modify logs pending your confirmation. If anything changes on your side, reply-all to ensure alignment.

Thanks — we’ll treat this as high priority and keep you updated as artifacts become available.

Tessa Morgan
